RECOMMEND: APPROVE, once you have read the report — AC-6 requires exactly that, so this gate is not fully closeable without you.

DECISION EFFECT: approving confirms the report answers your question and is usable as delivered. This is the one AC only you can satisfy. Rejecting sends it back with feedback on what the report is missing.

WHERE THE REPORT IS: functions/backfill-reports/060-report/report.md, on this machine. It is gitignored, not committed, and its supporting scripts are gitignored too — verified directly, not just claimed. It is NOT in a Google Doc; the ideation-stage finding that your Drive connector is bound to your work account, not your personal one, made a Doc the worse privacy option, so it landed local instead, matching 061's own precedent. If you want it as a Doc or want it moved somewhere else you can reach from your phone, say so and I will treat that as a finding to route.

WHAT THE REPORT DOES, without any figure in it: leads with the one screen you can reproduce yourself (Reports, Annual, 2025, filtered to your own payer, against unfiltered 2023) — that single filter already closes most of the apparent gap. Then it isolates same-person-same-categories spending with a small reproducible script, since Reports has a payer filter but no category filter, and states why a script was chosen over hand-summing. Then a full 25-category table, four labelled reasons split between recording-coverage and open questions, Babies presented to you as an unresolved decision rather than an answer, the mortgage lever sized with the honest caveat that entity 064 has not landed so the figure is sourced directly from your mortgage schedule, 2024 treated only as partial-window shape corroboration, and a three-step glide path checked against your own Coast FIRE Annual tab.

ONE THING I VERIFIED MYSELF RATHER THAN TAKING THE STAGE REPORT'S WORD: I read the whole report. Its independently-recomputed like-for-like ratio and mortgage-gap-share match ideation's numbers exactly, which is the reproducibility the report claims for itself, demonstrated rather than asserted.

A PROCESS NOTE, not a decision point: this entity's spec stage did what a code-shipping feature's build stage normally does — produced the actual deliverable, not just a specification of one — because the deliverable IS a report, not code. That is a deliberate departure from this workflow's usual shape, made explicitly in the entity rather than silently. I will work out with you what the next stage looks like once this gate closes, since there is no code for a build stage to write here.

artifacts.summary:
SPEC OUTPUT: a private analysis report answering the captain's question — why 2025 looks roughly double 2023-2024 — delivered as a local gitignored file rather than a tracked repo artifact, with the entity recording only its location.

CHECKLIST: 4 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed. Report written and verified gitignored (git check-ignore -v and git status both confirm); like-for-like mechanism settled as a reproducible script rather than hand-summing, chosen because every other measurement in this entity already reads the same source through the same credential path; Babies presented as an explicit open decision, not resolved; mortgage lever sized with its sourcing caveat stated (064 has not landed).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: six. AC-1 through AC-5 offline-verifiable against the report and its reproducible backing scripts; AC-6 interactive — the captain reading the report and confirming it answers her question, which is the check this gate performs. AC-1 (private, gitignored, entity records only the location), AC-2 (no money figure of the captain's in the entity, a commit message, or any tracked repo file), AC-3 (like-for-like mechanism settled and reproducible), AC-4 (Babies presented as a decision, not resolved), AC-5 (mortgage lever sized, correctly sourced given 064's current status, glide path proposed against the app's own figures and the captain's own Coast FIRE Annual tab) were all independently verified by the first officer reading the delivered report directly, not taken from the stage report's claim alone.

WHAT THE REPORT ESTABLISHES, in ratios and shares only, no figure: the payer-only filter (Reports' own screen, no script needed) already brings the apparent doubling down substantially. The like-for-like restriction (same payer, same 14 shared categories, via the reproducible script) shows spending on the directly-comparable part of the record FELL — the "roughly double" is not a spending increase there. The gap decomposes across new categories entering the record, with Mortgage and a new Babies category the two largest single terms, Mortgage self-evidently a coverage effect (a cost already being paid) and Babies explicitly NOT self-evident, framed as the captain's call. The single largest correctable lever is the mortgage gap, sized against the House tab schedule directly since entity 064 has not yet landed. 2024 is used only for a same-window partial-year comparison, never as a bare annual total, per 061 Finding 4's 53-day gap. The glide path is checked against the captain's own current Coast FIRE Annual tab rather than the archive workbook's outdated projection table, and states plainly that the 2025 app-total-equals-life-spend equality the whole reversal rests on does not extend to 2023 or 2024 without the same archive access Round B would need.

WHAT THIS SPEC EXPLICITLY DOES NOT RESOLVE, left for the captain or a later round: Babies' provenance; what NT$1.2M actually counted historically, folded together with 2023/2024's own figure provenance as the same underlying question, both requiring archive workbook access currently blocked; anything before 2022; whether a standing Reports feature for this kind of comparison is worth building later, named as a possible future filed idea, not decided here.

PROCESS NOTE: this entity's spec stage produced the deliverable itself rather than only a specification, because the deliverable is a report rather than code — stated explicitly in the stage report rather than silently departing from the workflow's usual build-stage shape.
